beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process updates it through shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR starts by turning the low-resolution image into features the rest of the system can keep dense. The dense field is partitioned into windows before the compact thought process reads and updates it. The DQ-CTM thought process runs for repeated ticks, with the same parameters shared across those ticks. The recurrence returns to the thought stage itself, so the loop is local to the updater. The decoder turns the updated dense representation back into the super-resolved output.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier with compact recurrent thought

stages.label: DQ-CTM thought
stages.note: Shared ticks read and update the carrier

params.note: The recurrence stays inside the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first creates dense features from the low-resolution image, then partitions that dense field into token windows without discarding it.
beats.narration: The carrier begins as a dense feature field produced from the low-resolution input. The encoder is the part that maps the image into that feature field. The low-resolution image is the input being encoded. The window partition then converts the dense field into tokens for the thought process while keeping the carrier intact.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before it becomes window tokens

terms.label: window partition that keeps every token

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters, it is the second largest of the five listed methods.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read as a cost, not just as a compactness claim. CATANet is the smallest method listed at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN and IMDN are also smaller than DQ-CTM-SR. DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger, while the source says ThinkSR is competitive with CNN baselines and behind recent lightweight transformers.
